draft.body:
Meditation at Constitution Gardens: A Morning of Stillness in Washington, DC

On Sunday, September 20, 2026, several hundred people gathered at Constitution Gardens in Washington, DC, for a morning of meditation and shared stillness. The forecast had called for scattered showers, overcast skies, and the possibility of thunder later in the day. The evening before, volunteers wondered quietly how many people would choose to sit on wet grass at half past eight on a Sunday morning.

Several hundred did.

A Community That Came Prepared

People arrived with umbrellas, folding chairs, yoga mats, and rain ponchos. Because two races were closing roads across the city that morning, some chose running shoes and walked in rather than drove. Some people came alone and settled at the edge of the field. Others brought children. Each person arrived with their own morning, their own circumstances, and perhaps their own reasons for needing a pause.

At 8:30 a.m., on a field in the middle of a city that rarely stops, everybody stopped together.

Stillness in the Middle of the City

Meditation does not require perfect conditions. A clear forecast can be welcome, but practice also meets us in the conditions already present: the clouds overhead, the damp grass beneath us, the sounds of a city nearby, and the thoughts and feelings we bring with us.

That morning at Constitution Gardens, the gathering itself became a quiet reminder that stillness is possible even when the day seems uncertain. For a little while, people from across the community shared the same intention—to sit, to breathe, and to be present.

“May you be at ease. Now and always.”

This wish held special meaning on a morning when simply arriving took patience and effort. Ease does not always mean that circumstances are easy. It can also mean making room for the moment as it is, with kindness toward ourselves and one another.

Gratitude for a Shared Morning of Meditation

We are grateful to everyone who came, to the volunteers who helped make the gathering possible, and to every person who offered their presence to this shared morning of meditation in Washington, DC. May the calm and connection cultivated at Constitution Gardens continue to support us as we return to the pace of daily life.

May all beings be happy and at ease.
